Core multipart create, upload, paginated listing, selected-part completion, abort, UploadPartCopy, and SigV4-presigned UploadPart flows are supported. Conditional completion headers and Object Lock parameters on multipart initiation remain outside the certified subset.

S3 versioning and Object Lock are mutually exclusive with GCS and Azure data-protection ownership of the same bucket. S3 enable/suspend and protected mutations return InvalidBucketState 409 without mutation while a foreign mode is active; enabling S3 never converts or unlocks that bucket.
Configuration round-trips are covered, but requester-pays billing semantics are not emulated.

Retention and legal hold protect the retained version while versioned PUT/COPY and simple DELETE may create a new version or marker. Current-version tag mutations are blocked while retained; version-scoped tagging, IAM-authorized governance bypass, and full bucket Object Lock control-plane parity are explicitly unsupported without mutation.
SSE request headers are validated and surfaced, but SQRZL does not perform provider-equivalent encryption key management.

Browser-style POST uploads and the accepted DeleteObjects subset are covered by contract tests, but not part of the SDK certification gate. DeleteObjects validates XML schema nesting, the 1000-object limit, and Content-MD5 before mutation and reports per-entry ETag/Object Lock failures.

Delete Container enters a durable local deleting-name state, hides the container immediately, and rejects same-name recreation until lazy purge. Data-plane deletion rejects active or malformed fail-closed WORM protection across current blobs, snapshots, and versions before scheduling or reclaiming bytes. Unsupported container subresources return FeatureNotSupported before namespace mutation. Production control-plane garbage-collection timing is not claimed.

Azure local versioning/soft-delete mode is mutually exclusive with S3 and GCS data-protection ownership of the same container. Conflicting activation, protected mutation, or foreign version access returns FeatureVersionMismatch 409 without mutation. Selected previous-version and snapshot mutations are either handled by the supported delete path or rejected before changing the current blob. Put Block List preserves Committed, Uncommitted, and Latest selectors and reports real block sizes. Unimplemented blob subresources return FeatureNotSupported before ordinary blob CRUD can run.

Blob SAS read, create, write, and delete permissions are verified, including staging and committing a multi-block upload through one SDK-generated SAS. Account SAS and service-level SAS operations remain outside this subset.

Put Block payloads are disk-staged and Put Block List composes them without materializing the complete blob. The emulator enforces 4,000 MiB per block, 100,000 uncommitted blocks, 50,000 committed blocks, the approximately 190.7 TiB block-blob ceiling, and cleanup on commit, overwrite, or rejected sessions.
Append blob writes persist locally, but append-position and service-property edge cases are not SDK-certified.
Page blob writes persist locally, but sparse-page and sequence-number parity are not SDK-certified.

Lease enforcement is covered for core local flows, including preserving an active lease across successful Put Blob and Put Block List replacements. Provider timing and break/renew edge cases are simplified.
Snapshot reads and deletes are covered for local flows, but snapshot lifecycle parity is not fully certified.

Local Locked policies cannot be shortened, unlocked, or deleted; invalid requests and malformed durable WORM state fail without mutation. With Azure versioning enabled, Put Blob and Put Block List create a new current version while retaining the protected predecessor and return the new version identity; without versioning, the same protected overwrites fail closed. Protected current blobs, snapshots, and versions block data-plane container scheduling and purge. Provider authorization and production governance/compliance control-plane parity are not claimed.

The accepted JSON upload checksum subset validates base64 big-endian CRC32C supplied in multipart object metadata and in X-Goog-Hash on media or final resumable requests. Malformed, conflicting, mismatched, and unsupported checksum algorithms fail before mutation; a failed final resumable checksum leaves the session retriable. A separate third multipart checksum part and MD5 validation remain explicitly rejected rather than approximated. Current-generation JSON metadata, media, and delete selectors are accepted only when they equal the stored generation; historical generation access remains unsupported.

Signed URL V2 validation and canonicalized x-goog-* extension headers are covered. GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 validates canonical path, query, signed headers, scope, expiry, and payload mode for signed resumable initiation. RSA service-account signed URLs remain outside this HMAC subset.

GOOG1 V2 HMAC authorization canonicalizes x-goog-* extension headers by lowercasing and sorting names, merging duplicate values in request order, excluding customer-supplied encryption key headers, and appending the required newline. Official SDK positive qualification is not yet in the certification gate.

JSON and XML resumable sessions persist across restart, accept repeated 256 KiB-aligned non-final chunks and status probes, combine CRC32C incrementally, compose on disk, expire after seven days, and enforce the 5 TiB object ceiling. Initiation supports object name, contentType, string metadata, and GOOG4 HMAC signed URLs; unsupported writable metadata fields such as cacheControl return 501 instead of being silently ignored.

Unlocked bucket-retention and 7-to-less-than-90-day soft-delete configuration are locally covered and are mutually exclusive with S3 or Azure data-protection ownership of the bucket; conflicting activation returns FAILED_PRECONDITION 409 without mutation. Retention-policy locking, per-object retention, writable server-owned policy fields, and disabling an enabled soft-delete policy are explicitly rejected and are not claimed as compatible.

Current-object CRUD decodes object paths exactly once and preserves empty path components. OCI version-scoped object operations are explicitly rejected as unsupported without reading or deleting the current object. OCI RSA-SHA256 request signatures validate the configured tenancy/user/fingerprint key ID, required signed headers, canonical signing lines, request-target integrity, and a five-minute clock window using a configured PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 public key. Additional OCI authorization policy semantics are outside the local emulator.

UploadPart payloads are disk-staged and complete manifests compose without loading the full object. The emulator enforces 10 MiB non-final parts, 50 GiB per part, 10,000 parts, a 10 TiB object ceiling, and supports Object PAR direct PUT plus native PAR multipart initiation. Unlisted parts require explicit exclusion; selective commits and conditional completion return 501 without consuming the session.

The accepted SMTP subset is plaintext EHLO/HELO, strict angle-bracket MAIL FROM and RCPT TO paths (including the RFC 5321 null reverse path), DATA, RSET, NOOP, and QUIT. SMTP AUTH, STARTTLS, relay/delivery, DSN semantics, and other extensions are unsupported; capture is atomic across recipient mailboxes.

The accepted SendGrid v3 Mail Send subset covers personalizations with to/cc/bcc, message or personalization sender/subject/headers, plain/HTML content, reply_to/reply_to_list, and base64 attachments. Recipient and personalization limits, global recipient uniqueness, reserved headers, content ordering, and the less-than-30-MB limit are enforced before atomic fan-out. Templates, substitutions, custom arguments, scheduling, tracking/settings, categories, ASM, batch IDs, IP pools, and sandbox delivery are explicitly rejected rather than ignored.

Outbound creation accepts only To, From or MessagingServiceSid, optional Body, up to 10 absolute HTTP(S) MediaUrl values, and a safety-allowlisted StatusCallback. Account/Messaging Service SIDs, E.164 values, media, 1600-character body limit, initial accepted/queued status, and Twilio error envelopes are validated before capture. Other create parameters, TwiML execution, remote media fetching, WhatsApp, RCS, voice, scheduling, automatic delivery timing, and provider management APIs are unsupported.

Only Query API Publish to a direct E.164 PhoneNumber is accepted, with raw messages or MessageStructure=json SMS/default selection and up to 10 documented MessageAttributes (including SMS SenderID and SMSType). Unknown/non-string structured protocol entries are ignored and duplicate JSON keys are rejected as SNS specifies. Topic/target publishing, FIFO parameters, fan-out, subscriptions, production certificate signing, and management APIs are unsupported.

Supports the documented JSON fields for SendTextMessage and SendMediaMessage, including DryRun without mutation and exactly one optional S3 media URI for MMS; provider patterns, ranges, maps, operation targets, 200 success, and AWS 400 error classes are enforced. Inbound MMS, automatic delivery timing, remote media fetching, voice operations, RCS, and provider management APIs are unsupported.

The accepted SES v2 SendEmail subset is Content.Simple with Destination, FromEmailAddress, ReplyToAddresses, subject/body charset metadata, and up to 15 non-reserved custom headers. Content.Raw, Content.Template, Simple attachments, tags, configuration sets, feedback forwarding, tenant fields, and other top-level options are explicitly rejected. SigV4 is validated for the local endpoint, but IAM, identities, quotas, and every signing edge case are not certified.

ACS Email versions 2023-03-01, 2023-03-31, and 2025-09-01 accept official to/cc/bcc recipients (50 total), plain/HTML content, headers, replyTo, tracking control, and base64 regular/inline attachments within 10 MB. Operation-Id and five-minute repeatability semantics prevent overwrites or duplicate capture. Delivery, domain policy, events, suppression, quotas, and other ACS channels are outside scope.

ACS SMS versions 2021-03-07 and 2026-01-23 support 1-100 E.164 recipients, per-recipient repeatability results, and smsSendOptions for delivery-report enablement, tag, and 60-43200 second timeout. Mixed recipient results do not capture rejected recipients; unexpected persistence failures roll back the batch. messagingConnect, MMS, automatic delivery timing, and provider management APIs are unsupported.
Gmail is deferred because its OAuth2 and user-consent delivery model does not align with this SMTP/provider API-focused emulator in v1.
